t: Serbia was raised from a principality to a kingdom in 1882 under Milan I of the House of Obrenović.
The May Coup of 1903 killed King Alexander I and Queen Draga, brought Peter I of the Karađorđević dynasty to the throne and turned Serbia from Austria-Hungary towards Russia and France.
In the Balkan Wars of 1912–1913 Serbia's population rose from 2.9 million to 4.5 million and its territory by 81%, with Kosovo, Sandžak and Vardar Macedonia annexed.
dyk: By the beginning of the 1880s Serbia and Montenegro were the only European nations without railroads; one conservative deputy warned that building them would make Serbia suffer the fate of the Indians after the discovery of America.
ev: Milan I is proclaimed king and the Principality of Serbia becomes a kingdom
Serbia is defeated by Bulgaria in the Serbo-Bulgarian War after the Battle of Slivnitsa
Milan I abdicates and is succeeded by his son Alexander I
In the May Coup officers kill King Alexander I and Queen Draga; Peter Karađorđević becomes Peter I
Austria-Hungary imposes the Tariff War, the Pig war, on Serbia
Serbia fights the First and Second Balkan Wars and annexes Kosovo, Sandžak and Vardar Macedonia
Austro-Hungarian, German and Bulgarian troops occupy Serbia; the army retreats through Albania to Corfu
On 1 December Serbia unites with the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs to form the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes

f.successor: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (later the Kingdom of Yugoslavia)
